title: Hidden Sugar
subtitle: Free sugars hide behind many names.
description: An ingredient does not need to be called 'sugar' to act like sugar in your body. BOTIA reads the label and flags what it finds.
why_body: Products labelled 'natural', 'fit' or 'healthy' often use ingredients that behave like sugar while avoiding the word. Free sugars contribute to excess energy intake without providing specific nutrients. WHO recommends keeping free sugar intake below 10% of total daily energy — ideally below 5%.
what_body: BOTIA detects ingredients classified as free sugars or sugar-equivalent carbohydrates: maltodextrin, glucose syrup, corn syrup, fruit juice concentrate, hydrolyzed starch, dextrin, and others. They are technically not 'sugar' but your body processes them the same way.
can_1: Detect ingredients classified as free sugars by WHO criteria.
can_2: Flag sugar-equivalent carbohydrates hidden behind technical names.
can_3: Signal when a product marketed as healthy contains these ingredients.
cannot_1: Tell you the total sugar or carbohydrate content — check the nutrition label.
cannot_2: Determine whether this product suits your diet or will spike your blood sugar.
closing: To assess total intake, check the nutrition label under 'Carbohydrates — of which sugars'.
source_note: WHO Guideline: Sugars intake for adults and children (2015) · EFSA Scientific Opinion on dietary sugars (2022)
